## 固定收益市場主線

科技股強勁回升，降低投資人以政府公債避險的需求；市場同時重新押注聯準會緊縮，並承接季度再融資的首批供給，美國公債因而下跌。2年期殖利率上升5個基點至4.5615%，帶動曲線趨平；10年期上升2.46個基點至4.882%。油價再度大跌，壓低通膨補償，抵銷部分實質殖利率升幅，限制債市跌勢。

市場風險偏好普遍改善。Nasdaq 100上漲3.40%，半導體股上漲6.85%，美國高收益債利差明顯收窄。市場期待結束伊朗戰爭的進程有所突破，布蘭特原油期貨下跌6.26%至每桶$92.17。能源成本下降支撐股票，但上週因科技股下跌而湧入公債的避險買盤退潮，債市仍承受壓力。

聯準會官員最新談話仍將通膨置於政策展望的核心。芝加哥聯準銀行總裁Austan Goolsbee警告，AI建設熱潮開始呈現需求過熱的樣貌；里奇蒙聯準銀行總裁Tom Barkin則指出，企業成本壓力廣泛存在，仍須審慎推進緊縮。企業仍能取得融資，條件卻差異懸殊：Fox準備大規模投資等級債券再融資，Ecopetrol完成美元債發行，銀行則考慮以大幅折價出售Qualtrics債務。交易市場回暖之際，個別借款人及併購融資的壓力仍未消退。

## 美國公債回跌，通膨與再融資供給牽動行情

美國公債隨股市反彈而走弱。據Bloomberg盤中報導，2年期殖利率一度升至4.57%，約上升5個基點，之後回落至4.54%附近。油價下跌隨後使殖利率進一步遠離盤中高點。短天期公債另受到市場重新押注聯準會未來一年升息，以及3年期新券供給的壓力。

當日5年期殖利率上升3.18個基點至4.6767%，30年期上升1.38個基點至5.2783%。2年與10年期利差收窄2.54個基點至32.05個基點；2年與30年期利差則收窄3.62個基點至71.68個基點。跌勢集中在曲線前端，與當日交易報導所述的政策利率壓力回升一致。

通膨補償與實質殖利率的變化，顯示能源降價仍為債市提供相當支撐。10年期實質殖利率上升4.38個基點至2.6565%，同天期損益兩平通膨率下降1.92個基點至2.2255%。過去一週，10年期名目殖利率下降3.05個基點，其中通膨補償下降7.75個基點，實質殖利率則上升4.70個基點。過去一個月的債市漲幅仍大：名目殖利率下降35.58個基點，實質殖利率下降22.86個基點，損益兩平通膨率下降12.72個基點。

不同期間的推力並不相同。週一實質殖利率的升幅超過通膨補償的降幅；以一週而言，通膨補償下滑仍足以使名目公債整體上漲。SMBC Nikko策略師Joseph Abate與Monty Gandhi認為，殖利率若要持續跌破上週低點，可能需要更明確的經濟成長惡化跡象。當日股市回升，則降低了投資人對科技股帶動景氣下行的即時避險需求。

標普500上漲2.35%至7,549.94，VIX下跌22.31%至19.92。半導體股反彈尤其強勁，但指數仍較一個月前低20.19%。美元指數下跌0.60%至101.684，黃金期貨上漲1.83%至每盎司$4,149.50。股市復甦與能源價格持續調整的同時，受衝擊較大的科技股領域仍背負可觀跌幅。

美國財政部標售$580億3年期公債，得標殖利率為4.627%，較美東時間下午1時截標前的標售前交易殖利率高約0.5個基點。這一小幅尾差顯示需求略低於交易商預期，儘管得標殖利率比上次標售低約30個基點。直接投標人承接比例達創紀錄的35%，高於2月創下的31.9%。直接投標人的承接比重很高，但標售仍須以稍高的殖利率吸引需求。

Goolsbee週一在芝加哥談到通膨組成，提出另一項警訊：與能源或關稅關聯較小的服務價格也在上漲，AI資料中心建設則開始呈現傳統需求過熱的特徵。他形容經濟成長與勞動市場穩定，通膨過高才是主要經濟問題，並指出央行面對過熱通常需要積極因應。Goolsbee今年沒有政策投票權，將於2027年輪值投票。

Barkin另在南卡羅來納州表示支持升息，但強調需求面風險使升息步調必須謹慎。他具體指出，汽油、柴油、電腦晶片與健康保險等成本都在壓縮企業利潤，企業正積極評估客戶能承受多少漲價。即使原油降價，能源通膨透過企業定價擴散的可能性仍值得關注。

對AI如何影響支出，Barkin指出兩種不同風險。若投資報酬不如預期，企業投資、股價與仰賴資產財富支撐的消費都可能下降；若技術迅速成功，則可能取代更多勞工，削弱其支出。兩者都會使政策焦點轉向就業目標。不過，他懷疑個別地區的反對能否大幅阻止資料中心建設，因為開發商仍可找到願意接納的其他地點。他的基本判斷仍是消費可望保持韌性至年底，但這股力道能延續多久尚不確定。

週一公布的經濟數據顯示活動較強，家庭通膨預期則仍具黏著性。世界大型企業研究會10月就業趨勢指數由107.56升至108.36。9月批發庫存月增0.7%，高於市場預期的0.6%及修正後前值0.6%；批發銷售月增2.8%，前值修正為增長2.0%。紐約聯準銀行10月消費者通膨預期維持3.9%，高於預期的3.8%。

最新就業結構報導也使AI短期影響的討論更具體。管理、科學與技術顧問公司10月新增17,300個職位，為近兩年最大增幅；非住宅建築、專業承包商，以及電腦與電子產品製造商合計另增17,500個職位。摩根大通經濟學家Michael Feroli認為，通常被視為容易受AI影響的職業出現令人鼓舞的跡象，但提醒不宜過度解讀單月數據。牛津經濟研究院的Nancy Vanden Houten則認為，AI目前對整體勞動需求的增強作用似乎仍大於取代作用。各產業表現不一：金融業10月新增7,000個職位，但仍較一年前少99,000個；資訊業就業人數則年減119,000個。

## AI企業拓展融資，專案收益與成本受檢視

Alphabet正洽談首次發行港元及新加坡元債券，將融資來源拓展至更多亞洲市場。知情人士表示，公司考慮發行等值$10億至$15億的港元債，以及約等值$15億的新加坡元債，最快可能在本月進行，資金用於一般企業用途。磋商仍在進行，條件可能改變；Alphabet拒絕評論市場揣測。

Alphabet先前已在多個市場借款，這些潛在發行將進一步擴大其融資幣別。投資人正密切檢視科技業基礎設施承諾，對債權人而言，眼前的變化是大型科技借款人可能再增加一批供給。Akamai也在籌資，啟動兩筆各$11億的擬議可轉換優先債券，分別於2028年與2031年到期，預計用途包括部分償還2027年到期債券，以及支應雲端基礎設施服務業務。

BloombergNEF最新研究量化了資料中心開發商另一項再融資風險：2027年將有$134億固定利率美元債到期。假設信用利差不變，若全數依2026年10月的美國公債殖利率再融資，利率將提高2.85個百分點，每年利息支出至少增加$3.8億；實際成本仍取決於再融資當時的利率與利差。

更廣泛的到期壓力延伸至往後數年。BloombergNEF估計，未來五年內至少有$1兆資料中心借款到期，2030年以前到期的債務多數集中於八家公司，其中以Vantage Data Centers、Switch及Databank規模最大。新型雲端業者在2030至2032年間有$490億借款到期，約占其截至2026年9月未償借款的65%；CoreWeave與Nebius占這批到期債務的80%。

研究也指出，銀行對開發商的選擇更加審慎，可能限制再融資能力。Terawulf與Crusoe等大量投入建設的公司，面臨電網併聯排隊及技術勞工短缺，租金收入可能延後實現。若完工與收入遞延，債務義務仍須履行，就必須支應專案開始產生現金前的資金空窗。這項風險隨專案時程與融資結構而異，並不隨AI市場規模一致變化。

美國國會正在審議一項可能改變部分開發成本與效益的提案。《跨黨派美國可負擔性與就業法案》將加快發電與輸電設施許可，同時要求大型資料中心營運商負擔更多因自身需求而生的電網升級費用，並設置保障，避免大型專案失敗後由一般電力用戶承受相關成本。參議院預計週一開始辯論。

川普總統支持這項提案，參議員Sheldon Whitehouse認為，可兼顧可負擔性並提高資料中心的責任。環保團體與部分民主黨人士則反對其中可能削弱監督或促進化石燃料開發的條款。TD Cowen在選後將法案通過機率由選前的40%降至25%。提案一方面加速基礎設施審批，一方面可能要求申請用電容量的企業承擔更高比例的電網費用，能否通過及最終條文都將影響專案。

Nvidia的公司治理危機，也為這家產業核心供應商帶來不確定性。執行長黃仁勳承認與一名女子有婚外情後，董事會啟動調查；報導指該女子疑為中國間諜，北京否認間諜指控。當日美國半導體股普遍大漲，Nvidia股價仍下跌約4.3%。

最新報導指出，Nvidia法務長曾介入美國政府對Megaspeed International涉嫌晶片走私的調查。這家新加坡客戶與本次爭議有關，否認不法行為，並表示遵守相關法規。Nvidia先前則稱，內部調查未發現晶片遭轉運至未獲授權去向的證據。公司調查與出口管制審視同時涉及重要客戶關係與這家晶片供應龍頭的領導層，商業影響仍未明朗。

日本半導體業另有一筆具體併購。三井化學同意以¥1.84兆、約合$120億，向日本投資公司收購JSR，並獲日本政策投資銀行（DBJ）支持。DBJ將出資¥2,000億取得股權，之後轉為無投票權特別股。日本整合關鍵晶片材料業務之際，這筆交易將使主要光阻劑供應商JSR納入三井化學。消息公布後，三井化學股價在東京一度下跌15%。

## 企業融資分化：新債發行與承銷壓力並存

Fox於週五完成$220億的Roku收購後，開始就約$80億投資等級債券舉行投資人電話會議。知情人士表示，發行可能涵蓋約七種年期，介於3年至40年，最快本週進行。Fox為支付收購案現金部分，已動用$84億過橋融資，另向摩根士丹利取得$20億定期貸款；擬議債券將以較長期融資取代暫時性的併購資金。

哥倫比亞國家控制的石油公司Ecopetrol已完成部分併購融資的轉換，發行$20億、2034年到期債券，價格99.388，殖利率7.98%，低於初步洽談的約8.35%。部分資金將提前償還收購巴西Brava Energia控制股權所用的過橋貸款。這筆已完成的收購代表公司在巴西投入$12億擴張，Brava每日產量約80,000桶。

Credicorp分析師Orlando Barriga認為，Brava可增加產量、儲量及地域分散性，哥倫比亞即將上任政府支持探勘的立場，也降低政策不確定性。他的看法正面，但投資選擇日益審慎，並指出高布蘭特油價與煉油利潤有助現金創造。Ecopetrol透過本次發債取得融資，投資人仍持續評估哥倫比亞財政赤字與公司擴大的營運版圖。

當日美國高收益債整體利差明顯收窄。計入配息，HYG報酬率約0.36%，LQD約0.13%，EMB為0.63%。不過，個別併購債務仍顯示融資風險偏好的復甦有其限制。

以摩根大通為首的銀行正考慮在高收益債市場大幅折價出售近$20億Qualtrics債務。知情人士表示，初步構想為票息至少8%、發行價格約面額的85%。投資人會議安排於本週，可能在下週感恩節前出售。銀行正試圖分銷其持有約$50億債務中的一部分。

Qualtrics最新營運成績出爐後，銀行重新展開債務推介。知情人士透露，第3季營收由第2季的$7.18億降至$7.11億，年增率則由前兩季的6%與7%降至2%。過去四季創造現金超過$11億，其中第3季為$2.3億、第2季為$1.79億。公司仍在整合以$67.5億交易估值收購的Press Ganey Forsta。

承銷銀行3月在軟體股拋售期間中止先前的債務分銷，自行提供收購資金。目前討論的安排是，除非所有貸款人同意出售，否則其餘債務至少再持有六個月。Qualtrics現有貸款於2030年到期，利率為美國基準利率加2.25個百分點，週一報價為面額的81%至83%。擬議債券的價格與票息屬於新一輪分銷協商；現有貸款報價則是另一筆債務的條件。

Fullscript的融資也在尋找替代管道。槓桿貸款初步洽談未能吸引足夠需求後，私募信貸業者正商談提供$13億貸款，支應L Catterton與Altas Partners收購多數股權。摩根士丹利領銜的銀行原以基準利率加碼最多4個百分點承銷融資，仍承諾為預計週二交割的交易提供資金。若直接貸款談成，將取代這些銀行承諾。

申報資料顯示，Apollo與Blue Owl投資了Fullscript現有私募債務，其利率加碼為4.5個百分點，與銀行承銷的加碼上限不同；潛在替代融資條件仍在磋商。融資管道選定後又轉向的情況並不常見，反映投資人需求改變時，先前作出的承諾可能難以分銷。

達拉斯與紐約聯準銀行宣布，將對規模$1.8兆的私募信貸產業進行新調查，涵蓋第3季融資供給情況、放貸標準、借款需求、契約文件與新貸款核准情形，並依EBITDA將借款人分組，範圍從低於$3,000萬至超過$1億。受訪管理機構須至少有$5,000萬專門用於對非投資等級企業直接放貸。結果預計於2027年第1季公布，不作為監理用途。

隔夜新聞中的澳洲週二消息指出，澳洲證券投資委員會（ASIC）確認，已對Bathla Group相關事務展開正式調查。這家開發商8月倒閉，負債約A$34億，多數欠款對象為私募信貸基金。委員Simone Constant區分了Bathla調查與對私募貸款機構的查核，後者尚未進入正式調查。

ASIC最新檢視24檔私募信貸基金，發出六項暫停令，並將多起案件移送執法。22檔有費用資料的基金中，只有兩檔將利息與借款人費用的全部經濟利益交付投資人。監管機關指出，複雜架構與不完整揭露掩蓋利益衝突。澳洲規模A$2,500億的私募信貸產業因而面臨更具體的費用與行為問題檢視。

泰晤士水務債權人支持一項過渡性展期，擬將2027年到期的超優先、A類與B類債務延至2028年3月。持有逾£120億擔保債務的債權人支持提案，但仍須透過法院監督重整。公司也正尋求另外£24億緊急貸款。展期可爭取協商時間，且不使公司承諾接受London & Valley Water債權人團體構想中的資本重整；該團體尚未提出完整方案。債權人預計12月表決，法院聽證排在1月。

中國市場則重新聚焦華發境內AAA評等與債券價格的落差。聯合資信及給予華發BBB評等的惠譽，均將其列入負向觀察。部分人民幣債券成交價低於面額70%，殖利率超過10%。華發仍持續履行債券償付義務，珠海國資監管機關也承諾全力支持，但$620億借款與獲利放緩仍令投資人擔憂。評等問題部分在於，預期中的國家支持能否及時到位以履行債務；評等維持、債券持續償付與困境定價同時存在。

## 各國通膨與財政選擇改變融資環境

墨西哥10月通膨數據加深了對央行近期降息的爭論。整體通膨年增率由3.45%升至3.75%，高於Bloomberg調查所有預估值，預估中位數為3.65%；核心通膨由3.75%升至3.80%，也高於3.78%的預期。電力、航空運輸、番茄及家用瓦斯是主要推力，公布的價格漲幅分別為18.51%、26.36%、9.68%與3.67%。

上週反對降息的央行理事Galia Borja週一表示，自己賦予通膨風險的權重高於其他同僚。不過，她不認同這次降息過早的說法，指出央行從9月起就已釋出訊號，並認為12月維持利率不變的可能性很高。總裁Victoria Rodriguez Ceja則表示，經濟活動優於預期，但仍有閒置產能，限制了需求面的通膨壓力。

民間經濟學家對通膨走勢較不放心。Banco Base的Gabriela Siller以披索貶值與服務價格壓力為由，不認為明年通膨能降至3%；凱投宏觀的William Jackson預期，整體與核心通膨都將超過央行對第4季3.7%的預測。通膨意外偏高後，分歧集中在回歸目標的過程能否持續，而央行目前的政策指引仍是較長時間維持利率不變。

巴西央行週一調查顯示，經濟學家轉向預期更長的利率暫停期。他們連續第二週調高年底Selic利率預測，從13.5%升至13.75%，並將2027年底通膨預估由4.76%上修至4.9%，相較之下，通膨目標為3%。總統魯拉連任後首次發表電視談話，承諾維持財政規則、延續社會計畫，並尋求將投資提高至GDP的20%以上，但未提出相應的具體減支或增收措施。總統試圖安撫投資人對債務的疑慮之際，調查中的通膨與利率預期均向上修正。

印度債市討論聚焦於流動性回收與進一步升息預期的交互影響。銀行體系現金盈餘由9月初的11兆盧比降至11月5日的2.3兆盧比。此前僑民存款計畫帶來美元，銀行將其兌換為盧比；印度央行之後透過先賣後買外匯交換，以及1.25兆盧比的公開市場售債回收資金。IDFC First Bank與德意志銀行預期，未來數月最多還會升息75個基點。

5年與10年期殖利率利差約32個基點，低於8月底的37個基點。Quantum基金經理人Sneha Pandey認為，更積極回收流動性，加上預期終端利率上升，可能使這段利差短暫降至零，甚至輕微倒掛。油價下跌則提供相反方向的支撐：上週5年期殖利率下降33個基點，大於10年期的22個基點降幅。

另據知情人士，印度央行稽核人員已要求部分銀行，對遠期債券交易採用第3等級估值輸入值。這類輸入值是在可觀察市場資訊有限時仰賴內部假設，其分類可能限制股利及監管資本。今年相關交易名目本金合計1.1兆盧比。銀行正與結算機構討論提供更多定價資訊，該機構也在測試電子交易平台，以提高透明度。

日本財政融資討論則增加了新發公債以外的資金選項。外匯資金特別會計2025會計年度盈餘約¥5.1兆，其中約¥3.1兆撥入下一年度的一般會計。相關準則通常要求至少保留30%作為匯率風險緩衝。提高撥款的提議可提供財源，但盈餘易受海外利率、日圓與干預需求影響。日本總合研究所經濟學家Takeshi Makita警告，不宜將其視為永久財源。

經濟產業省另提議擴大透過日本政策金融公庫進行的兩階段轉貸，納入大型銀行與地方銀行，並由政府吸收部分貸款損失。這些措施將支持高市推動的投資目標：截至2040會計年度，在17個戰略領域投入¥370兆公私部門資金。慶應義塾大學的土居丈朗提醒，損失最終可能轉入一般會計，但銀行若同時提供政府支持貸款與自有貸款，仍有誘因評估風險。高市以先前年度約¥40兆發債規模為參考，表示下一份預算可採類似做法。

匯率預測反映各方對這些融資所處利率環境的不同看法。TTT Moneycorp的Neil Parker預期，日圓年底約為155，明年為147；日本央行將把利率由1.25%升至至少2%，可能達2.25%，聯準會則在4.00%至4.25%左右停止升息。他預估，至明年年中至下半年，利差還會縮小約50個基點。Parker表示，若基礎通膨達2.6%或以上，可能加快政策反應；9月排除生鮮食品與能源的通膨率為2.4%。他的看法與另一位主要預測者認為日圓將貶向170的預期形成對照。

亞洲各幣別新債仍持續發行。波克夏海瑟威已委任瑞穗與美國銀行，視市場條件進行潛在日圓基準債發行。日本企業10月大量供給使利差擴大後，發債速度已放緩。中國則完成先前宣布在加拿大發行的人民幣綠色主權債，總額人民幣40億元，平均分為3年期與5年期，殖利率分別為1.4%與1.5%。訂單超過人民幣590億元，約為發行規模的14.75倍；財政部藉此在香港、澳門與倫敦以外，首次選擇另一個離岸人民幣發債地點取得資金。

歐洲方面，各國部長推進ECB接班程序，可能將總裁及Isabel Schnabel、Philip Lane的席次一併安排，目標在年底前決定。候選人Klaas Knot表示，面對無正當理由且失序的利差變動，ECB可動用包括大規模購債在內的危機工具。他認為目前沒有重大政策傳導障礙，且第二輪效應仍受控制，可能只需再做有限緊縮。這位普遍被視為鷹派的候選人，對通膨的評估較為有節制；現行ECB政策未因此改變。

## 油價下跌緩解成本，供給仍面臨風險

布蘭特原油跌至每桶$92.17，西德州原油下跌4.90%至$86.38，能源成本進一步下降。布蘭特油價較一週前低12.03%，外交進展的樂觀預期支撐這波跌勢。不過，美國國務卿Marco Rubio仍稱伊朗的談判要求不可接受；伊朗則表示，在遭美國攻擊威脅的情況下，沒有義務接受全面核監督，談判的一項核心障礙仍未解決。

路透調查提供了實際產量回升的證據。納入調查的11個OPEC成員國，10月每日產量估計為2,287萬桶，比9月增加138萬桶，增幅由沙烏地阿拉伯、科威特與伊拉克領銜。產量已恢復至2月戰前每日2,548萬桶的約90%。此前增產配額未能全數轉化為實際供給，原因包括衝突與出口限制，其中也涵蓋美國對伊朗船運的封鎖。

沙烏地阿拉伯國營媒體報導，麥地那地區的東西向輸油管遭到新一輪攻擊。能源部消息人士表示，局部火勢已撲滅，無人受傷，營運未受影響。荷莫茲海峽受限後，這條管線每日約將400萬桶原油改道輸往延布；據路透估計，相當於全球供給約4%。管線持續運作，維繫了一條重要替代出口路線，襲擊也凸顯基礎設施暴露的風險。

俄羅斯燃料供給則遭遇另一種中斷。路透報導，烏克蘭兩週內攻擊至少八座主要煉油廠後，部分地區再度實施配給。列寧格勒州州長Alexander Drozdenko通報，俄羅斯第二大煉油廠Kirishi夜間遇襲。卡累利阿將公路沿線汽油購買量限制為30公升、柴油50公升，並暫停向油桶售油。可運轉煉油產能減少，可能限制成品油出口，包括先前討論的柴油安排，但最新一輪全國產量損失尚未量化。

能源成本仍高，歐洲政府也在因應負擔問題。義大利核准自1月起實施18個月的計畫，補償燃氣發電業者TTF天然氣價格高於每MWh €58.9的差額。能源部長Pichetto Fratin估計，平均電力成本可減輕每MWh約€15。計畫多數資金來自對部分用戶提高系統費，以及生產商的分攤；能源公司反對限制成本轉嫁。TTF週一約每MWh €82，10月曾超過€104。

捷克政府核准一項因應能源市場異常壓力的立法提案，仍待國會審議。提案允許政府預算吸收部分電力與天然氣網路費用，並對生產商課徵超額利潤稅以支應紓困。義大利已核准的暫時補償與捷克提案，對家庭、生產商及政府的能源成本分配方式不同，最終帳單影響仍取決於措施運作及批發價格。

## 後續市場焦點

美國10月CPI將於週二美東時間上午8時30分公布。市場預期整體CPI月增0.3%，低於前月0.6%；核心CPI月增0.2%，低於前月0.3%。去年政府停擺干擾資料蒐集，因此本次不公布年增率。在Goolsbee警告需求過熱、Barkin指出企業廣泛轉嫁成本之後，除了預期整體通膨放緩，服務與商品各項月增幅的分布也將受到關注。

週二另有NFIB小企業樂觀指數，預估為97.7，前值97.9，之後公布ADP每週就業數據。Christopher Waller、Lorie Logan、Michelle Bowman與Jeffrey Schmid均有預定談話，他們的看法將補充對通膨持續性、緊縮步調，以及金融市場波動如何改變需求展望的討論。

美國財政部週二美東時間下午1時將標售$420億10年期公債，週四再標售$250億30年期公債，兩場標售之間的週三適逢退伍軍人節休市。下一場標售接在CPI之後，而3年期標售剛出現直接投標人承接比例創紀錄、但仍有小幅尾差的結果，市場對通膨的反應與新發公債需求將緊接著接受檢驗。

企業融資焦點包括Fox的潛在發債、預計週二交割的Fullscript收購案與替代直接貸款協商，以及Qualtrics的債務推介。Anthropic最快可能週二正式啟動IPO推介。這些交易將顯示，風險偏好回升如何轉化為成熟發行人、私募股權支持企業與AI籌資案的實際融資條件。

能源方面，下一項預定評估是週二EIA《短期能源展望》。外交進展之外，沙烏地出口基礎設施能否持續運作，以及俄羅斯維持成品油供給的能力，仍是各自影響價格路徑的因素。印度週四公布零售通膨，Bloomberg調查預估為6%，正好位於印度央行容忍區間上限。這項數據將檢驗，在國內通膨與流動性緊縮壓力下，油價下跌究竟能提供多少空間。

overall_summary.headline: 科技股反彈、聯準會緊縮預期回升，美國公債下跌
overall_summary.session_narrative:
科技股回升降低避險需求，市場重新押注聯準會緊縮，並承接再融資供給，美國公債回吐部分近期漲幅。2年期殖利率上升5個基點至4.5615%，10年期上升2.46個基點至4.882%，殖利率曲線趨平。10年期實質殖利率上升4.38個基點，損益兩平通膨率則下降1.92個基點，緩和名目公債跌勢。

Nasdaq 100上漲3.40%；市場期待結束伊朗戰爭的進程有所突破，布蘭特油價下跌6.26%至每桶$92.17。能源降價支撐股市，並壓低通膨補償。Goolsbee警告，AI建設開始呈現需求過熱的樣貌；Barkin則指出企業成本壓力廣泛存在，支持審慎推進緊縮。$580億3年期美國公債得標殖利率略高於標售前水準，直接投標人承接比例創紀錄。

美國高收益債利差明顯收窄，但融資條件仍不均。Fox準備約$80億投資等級債券再融資，Ecopetrol完成$20億美元債發行；銀行則考慮以約面額85%的價格出售近$20億Qualtrics債務。週二CPI與10年期公債標售將檢驗通膨展望及市場對新發公債的需求。
overall_summary.summary: 政府公債避險需求減少，加上政策利率壓力回升，推高實質殖利率；油價下跌則壓低通膨補償。企業仍能取得融資，但條件差異顯著。

## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasuries fell as a powerful recovery in technology shares reduced demand for government bonds as a hedge, while investors rebuilt expectations for Federal Reserve tightening and absorbed the first leg of the quarterly refunding. The two-year yield rose 5 basis points to 4.5615%, leading a flatter curve; the 10-year increased 2.46 basis points to 4.882%. A further plunge in oil helped restrain the selloff, with lower inflation compensation offsetting part of the increase in real yields.

The session brought a broad improvement in market risk appetite. The Nasdaq 100 gained 3.40%, semiconductor shares rose 6.85%, and U.S. high-yield spreads tightened noticeably. Brent futures fell 6.26% to $92.17 a barrel on hopes for progress toward ending the Iran war. That combination gave equities support from cheaper energy while leaving bonds exposed to the reversal of last week's technology-driven haven demand.

Fresh Fed remarks kept inflation central to the policy outlook. Chicago's Austan Goolsbee warned that the AI construction boom was beginning to resemble demand overheating, while Richmond's Tom Barkin described broad corporate cost pressures and a need for careful further tightening. Financing remained available, but on sharply differentiated terms: Fox prepared a large investment-grade refinancing, Ecopetrol completed a dollar issue, and banks explored a steep discount to distribute Qualtrics debt. The recovery in traded markets coincided with continuing pressure on particular borrowers and acquisition financings.

## Treasury Reversal Meets Inflation and Refunding Supply

The Treasury retreat developed alongside the equity rebound. Bloomberg's intraday account put the two-year yield as high as 4.57%, about 5 basis points higher, before a retreat toward 4.54%. Falling oil subsequently drew yields away from their session highs. Shorter maturities also faced renewed wagers on Fed increases over the next year and the arrival of three-year supply.

By the daily observation, five-year yields had risen 3.18 basis points to 4.6767%, while the 30-year added 1.38 basis points to 5.2783%. The two- to 10-year spread narrowed 2.54 basis points to 32.05 basis points. Across the longer two- to 30-year span, the gap contracted 3.62 basis points to 71.68 basis points. The concentration of losses near the front of the curve was consistent with the renewed policy-rate pressure described in the session's trading account.

The inflation decomposition showed how much support cheaper energy was still providing. The 10-year real yield rose 4.38 basis points to 2.6565%, while its breakeven inflation rate declined 1.92 basis points to 2.2255%. Over the week, the nominal 10-year yield was 3.05 basis points lower, comprising a 7.75-basis-point fall in inflation compensation and a 4.70-basis-point increase in real yields. The month-long rally remained substantial: the nominal yield was down 35.58 basis points, with real yields 22.86 basis points lower and the breakeven down 12.72 basis points.

Those horizons describe different balances. Monday's rise in real yields more than absorbed the day's further decline in inflation compensation. Across the week, lower inflation compensation still accounted for the net advance in nominal bonds. SMBC Nikko strategists Joseph Abate and Monty Gandhi argued that a sustained break below last week's yield lows might require clearer evidence of deterioration in growth. The day's equity recovery instead reduced the immediate demand for insurance against a technology-led downturn.

The S&P 500 gained 2.35% to 7,549.94, while the VIX fell 22.31% to 19.92. The semiconductor rebound was particularly large, although that index remained 20.19% below its month-earlier level. The Dollar Index declined 0.60% to 101.684, and gold futures gained 1.83% to $4,149.50 an ounce. The stock recovery and the continuing adjustment in energy prices therefore operated within a market still carrying substantial losses in its most exposed technology segment.

Treasury's $58 billion three-year auction cleared at 4.627%, about half a basis point above the yield in pre-auction trading immediately before the 1 p.m. Eastern bidding deadline. That small tail indicated demand slightly below dealer expectations, even though the yield was about 30 basis points below the previous auction's result. Direct bidders took a record 35%, exceeding February's previous record of 31.9%. A large direct allocation accompanied a modest concession at the clearing yield.

Goolsbee's Monday comments supplied a distinct warning about the composition of inflation. Speaking in Chicago, he said services prices less closely connected to energy or tariffs were also rising, while the AI data-center buildout was starting to look like conventional demand overheating. He described growth and the labor market as stable and excessive inflation as the principal economic problem. Central banks typically need to respond aggressively to overheating, he said. Goolsbee does not vote on policy this year but joins the voting rotation in 2027.

Barkin, speaking separately in South Carolina, also favored higher rates while emphasizing the risks to demand that warranted care over pace. His new detail concerned the breadth of costs businesses were trying to pass through: gasoline, diesel, computer chips and health insurance were all squeezing margins. He said companies were actively debating how much customers could absorb. The possibility that energy inflation spreads through corporate pricing remains relevant even as crude itself becomes cheaper.

He identified two different AI risks to spending. Disappointing returns could reduce business investment, equity prices and asset-supported consumption. Rapidly successful technology could instead displace more workers and weaken their spending. Either would shift attention toward the employment mandate. Barkin nevertheless doubted that opposition in particular jurisdictions would substantially halt data-center construction, arguing that developers could find other willing locations. His base case remained resilient consumption through year-end, with uncertainty about how long that strength would last.

Monday's economic releases added observations of firmer activity and sticky household inflation expectations. The Conference Board Employment Trends Index increased to 108.36 in October from 107.56. September wholesale inventories rose 0.7% month on month, above the 0.6% consensus and the revised 0.6% prior increase. Wholesale sales rose 2.8%, following a revised 2.0% gain. The New York Fed's consumer inflation-expectations reading held at 3.9% in October, against a forecast of 3.8%.

New reporting on the employment composition also sharpened the debate over AI's immediate effects. Management, scientific and technical consulting firms added 17,300 workers in October, their largest increase in almost two years. Nonresidential building construction, specialty contractors and computer and electronic-product manufacturers supplied another 17,500 jobs. JPMorgan economist Michael Feroli saw encouraging evidence in occupations often considered vulnerable to AI, while cautioning against drawing too much from one month. Oxford Economics' Nancy Vanden Houten judged that AI still appeared to be augmenting aggregate labor demand more than replacing it. The sectoral comparison was uneven: financial activities added 7,000 jobs in October but remained 99,000 below a year earlier, and information employment was down 119,000 over the year.

## AI Borrowers Expand Funding as Project Economics Face Scrutiny

Alphabet was discussing its first Hong Kong dollar and Singapore dollar bond offerings, extending the search for funding into additional Asian markets. People familiar with the talks said the company was considering the equivalent of $1 billion-$1.5 billion in Hong Kong dollars and around $1.5 billion in Singapore dollars, potentially as early as this month. Proceeds would serve general corporate purposes. Discussions continued and the terms could change; Alphabet declined to comment on market speculation.

The prospective issues would widen its currency access after earlier borrowing in several other markets. For creditors, the immediate news is another potential source of supply from a large technology borrower at a time when investors are scrutinizing infrastructure commitments. Akamai was also seeking capital, launching two proposed $1.1 billion convertible senior-note tranches due in 2028 and 2031. Its intended uses include partially repaying 2027 notes and funding its cloud-infrastructure services business.

A new BloombergNEF study quantified a separate refinancing exposure among data-center developers. It identified $13.4 billion of fixed-rate dollar debt maturing in 2027. Full refinancing at Treasury yields prevailing in October 2026 would increase interest rates by 2.85 percentage points and annual expenses by at least $380 million, assuming unchanged credit spreads. That is a benchmark-rate scenario based on October conditions; the cost ultimately incurred will depend on rates and spreads when borrowers refinance.

The broader maturity burden extends much further. BloombergNEF identified at least $1 trillion of data-center borrowings coming due within the next five years, with most debt maturing by 2030 concentrated among eight firms. Vantage Data Centers, Switch and Databank had the largest volumes. For neocloud companies, $49 billion matures between 2030 and 2032, approximately 65% of their outstanding borrowings as of September 2026. CoreWeave and Nebius account for 80% of those maturities.

The study also described banks becoming more selective about developers, potentially limiting refinancing capacity. Construction-heavy companies including Terawulf and Crusoe face interconnection queues and skilled-labor shortages that can delay rental income. When completion and revenue slip while debt obligations remain in place, the funding problem includes the interval before a project begins producing cash. This exposure varies with project schedules and financing structures, rather than following uniformly from the size of the AI market.

Congress was considering a proposal that could change some of those development economics. The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act would accelerate permitting for electricity generation and transmission while requiring large data-center operators to bear more of the grid-upgrade costs associated with their demand. It also includes protections intended to prevent ordinary electricity customers from inheriting costs when large projects fail. Senate debate was expected to begin Monday.

President Donald Trump endorsed the proposal, and Senator Sheldon Whitehouse argued it could combine affordability with greater data-center accountability. Environmental groups and some Democrats objected to provisions they believed could weaken oversight or promote fossil-fuel development. TD Cowen cut its estimated probability of enactment to 25% after the election from 40% beforehand. The proposal pairs faster infrastructure approvals with a potentially larger share of network costs for the companies seeking capacity, leaving both passage and final terms consequential for projects.

Nvidia's governance crisis added another source of uncertainty around the industry's central supplier. Its board launched an investigation after Chief Executive Jensen Huang acknowledged an affair with a woman identified in reports as a suspected Chinese spy. Beijing dismissed the spying allegations. Nvidia shares fell about 4.3% in the U.S. session even as the wider semiconductor market rallied.

Fresh reporting said Nvidia's general counsel had intervened in a U.S. government investigation of suspected chip smuggling by Megaspeed International, the Singapore-based customer connected to the controversy. Megaspeed denied wrongdoing and said it complied with relevant regulations. Nvidia had previously said its own inquiry found no evidence of diversion. The overlapping corporate investigation and export-control scrutiny concern a major customer relationship and the leadership of the industry's dominant chip supplier; their commercial consequences remain unresolved.

Japan supplied a separate, concrete semiconductor transaction. Mitsui Chemicals agreed to acquire JSR from Japan Investment Corp. for ¥1.84 trillion, or about $12 billion, with support from Development Bank of Japan. DBJ will contribute ¥200 billion in cash for a stake to be converted into nonvoting preferred shares. The acquisition brings a leading photoresist supplier into Mitsui Chemicals as Japan consolidates key chip-materials businesses. Mitsui Chemicals shares fell as much as 15% in Tokyo following the announcement.

## Credit Access Splits Between Issuance and Underwriting Strain

Fox began investor calls for roughly $8 billion of investment-grade bonds after completing its $22 billion Roku acquisition on Friday. People familiar with the plans said the offering could span about seven maturities from three to 40 years and come as soon as this week. Fox had borrowed $8.4 billion under a bridge facility for the cash portion of the takeover and obtained a further $2 billion term loan from Morgan Stanley. The proposed bonds would replace temporary acquisition funding with longer-term financing.

Ecopetrol completed that transition for part of its own acquisition financing. The Colombian state-controlled oil company sold $2 billion of notes due in 2034 at 99.388 to yield 7.98%, compared with initial discussions around 8.35%. Part of the proceeds will prepay a bridge loan associated with its purchase of a controlling stake in Brazil's Brava Energia. The completed acquisition represents a $1.2 billion expansion in Brazil, where Brava produces roughly 80,000 barrels a day.

Credicorp analyst Orlando Barriga said Brava adds production, reserves and geographic diversification, while the incoming Colombian administration's pro-exploration stance reduces policy uncertainty. His constructive but increasingly selective assessment also cited high Brent prices and refining margins as support for cash generation. The sale secured financing while investors continued to weigh Colombia's fiscal deficit and Ecopetrol's enlarged operating footprint.

Aggregate U.S. high-yield spreads tightened noticeably during the session. HYG returned about 0.36% including distributions, while LQD returned about 0.13% and EMB 0.63%. Individual acquisition debts nevertheless exposed limitations to the recovery in funding appetite.

Banks led by JPMorgan were considering a deeply discounted sale of nearly $2 billion of Qualtrics debt in the high-yield market. Early indications envisaged a coupon of at least 8% and an issue price around 85 cents on the dollar, according to people familiar with the talks. Meetings with investors were scheduled this week, with a possible sale next week before Thanksgiving. The banks are trying to distribute part of roughly $5 billion of debt they have been holding.

The new marketing effort follows Qualtrics' latest operating results. Revenue slipped to $711 million in Q3 from $718 million in Q2, people familiar with the figures said. Annual revenue growth slowed to 2%, following 6% and 7% in the preceding two quarters. Cash generation over the last four quarters exceeded $1.1 billion, including $230 million in Q3 and $179 million in Q2. The company continues to integrate Press Ganey Forsta, acquired in a transaction valued at $6.75 billion.

Underwriters had halted an earlier distribution attempt in March during the software selloff and funded the acquisition themselves. They are now discussing retaining the remaining debt for at least six months unless all lenders approve a sale. Qualtrics' existing loan, due in 2030 and paying 2.25 percentage points over the U.S. benchmark, was quoted at 81-83 cents on Monday. The proposed bond price and coupon reflect negotiations over a new distribution; the existing loan's quotation concerns a different obligation.

Fullscript's financing was also seeking another route. Private-credit firms were in talks to supply a $1.3 billion loan for L Catterton and Altas Partners' purchase of a majority stake after preliminary discussions failed to attract enough leveraged-loan demand. Morgan Stanley-led banks had underwritten the financing at a maximum margin of 4 percentage points over the benchmark and remained committed to fund the transaction, expected to close Tuesday. A direct loan would replace those commitments.

Apollo and Blue Owl are invested in Fullscript's existing private debt, which carries a margin of 4.5 percentage points, according to filings. That existing margin differs from the banks' underwriting ceiling; terms for the prospective replacement financing were still under discussion. The unusual switch after a funding route had been selected illustrates how commitments made earlier can become difficult to distribute when investor appetite changes.

The Dallas and New York Fed banks announced a new survey of the $1.8 trillion private-credit industry. It will examine availability, lending standards, borrower demand, documentation and new-loan approvals in Q3, separating borrowers by size using EBITDA bands from below $30 million to above $100 million. Eligible managers must have at least $50 million dedicated to direct lending to sub-investment-grade companies. Findings are due in Q1 2027 and will not be used for supervisory purposes.

In a Tuesday Australian update within the overnight news flow, ASIC confirmed a formal investigation into Bathla Group's affairs. The developer collapsed in August owing around A$3.4 billion, largely to private-credit funds. Commissioner Simone Constant distinguished the Bathla investigation from inquiries concerning private lenders, where no formal investigation had begun.

ASIC's latest review of 24 private-credit funds produced six interim stop orders and multiple enforcement referrals. Of 22 funds with fee information, only two passed the full economic benefit of interest and borrower fees to investors. The regulator identified conflicts obscured by complex structures and incomplete disclosure. The findings add specific conduct and fee concerns to scrutiny of Australia's A$250 billion industry.

Thames Water's creditors backed an interim extension that would move 2027 maturities on super-senior, Class A and Class B debt to March 2028. Holders of more than £12 billion of secured debt supported the proposal, which requires a court-supervised restructuring. Thames is also seeking another £2.4 billion of emergency loans. The extension would provide negotiating time without committing the utility to the London & Valley Water creditor group's prospective recapitalization, whose full proposal remains outstanding. Creditors are due to vote in December, with a court hearing in January.

In China, new scrutiny focused on the gap between Huafa's domestic AAA rating and its bond prices. China Lianhe and Fitch, which rates the company BBB, both had it on negative watch. Some yuan notes traded below 70% of face value with yields above 10%. Huafa continued meeting bond payments, and Zhuhai's state-asset regulator pledged full support, while its $62 billion of borrowings and slower profits sustained investor concern. The rating question turns partly on whether expected state support arrives in time for obligations; the maintained grade and continuing bond payments coexist with distressed market pricing.

## National Inflation and Fiscal Choices Reshape Funding

Mexico's October inflation release strengthened the debate over Banxico's recent easing. Annual headline inflation rose to 3.75% from 3.45%, above every estimate in a Bloomberg survey whose median was 3.65%. Core inflation increased to 3.80% from 3.75%, also exceeding the 3.78% forecast. Electricity, air transport, tomatoes and household gas were the leading contributors, with reported price increases of 18.51%, 26.36%, 9.68% and 3.67%, respectively.

Board member Galia Borja, who opposed last week's cut, said Monday that she had assigned more weight to inflation risks than colleagues. She nevertheless rejected the characterization that the reduction was premature, noting it had been signaled since September, and considered an unchanged December rate highly likely. Governor Victoria Rodriguez Ceja said activity had exceeded expectations but slack remained, limiting demand-side inflation.

Private economists were less comfortable with the trajectory. Banco Base's Gabriela Siller cited peso depreciation and services pressures in rejecting the prospect of inflation reaching 3% next year. Capital Economics' William Jackson expected both headline and core inflation to exceed Banxico's 3.7% Q4 forecast. The disagreement concerns the durability of convergence after an upside surprise, with the bank's extended-hold guidance remaining the immediate policy position.

Brazil's Monday central-bank survey moved toward a longer pause. Economists raised their year-end Selic forecast to 13.75% from 13.5%, a second successive weekly increase, and lifted their end-2027 inflation estimate to 4.9% from 4.76%, against a 3% target. In his first televised address after reelection, Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva pledged to preserve fiscal rules while sustaining social programs and seeking investment above 20% of GDP. He offered no specific spending cuts or revenue measures to accompany that commitment. The new survey showed forecasters marking up inflation and interest-rate expectations as the president sought to reassure investors about debt.

India's bond debate centered on the interaction of liquidity withdrawal with further expected tightening. The banking cash surplus had fallen to 2.3 trillion rupees on November 5 from 11 trillion rupees in early September. RBI sell-buy currency swaps and 1.25 trillion rupees of open-market bond sales had drained funds after a diaspora deposit program brought dollars that banks exchanged for rupees. IDFC First Bank and Deutsche Bank expected as much as another 75 basis points of rate increases in coming months.

The five- to 10-year yield gap was about 32 basis points, compared with 37 basis points at end-August. Quantum fund manager Sneha Pandey said more aggressive liquidity withdrawal and a higher expected terminal rate could temporarily flatten that gap to zero or produce mild inversion. Last week's 33-basis-point decline in five-year yields, exceeding the 10-year's 22-basis-point fall as crude dropped, shows the opposing influence of energy relief on that outlook.

Separately, RBI auditors had told some banks to use Level 3 valuation inputs for bond forwards, people familiar with the discussions said. Those inputs rely on internal assumptions where observable market information is limited, and the classification can constrain dividends and regulatory capital. Notional trades totaled 1.1 trillion rupees this year. Banks were discussing more pricing information with the clearinghouse, which was testing an electronic trading platform to improve transparency.

Japan's fiscal-financing discussion added detail on resources outside new bond issuance. The foreign-exchange special account generated about ¥5.1 trillion of surplus in fiscal 2025, with around ¥3.1 trillion transferred to the following year's general account. Guidelines generally preserve at least 30% as a currency-risk buffer. Proposals to increase transfers could provide funding, but the account's profits are sensitive to overseas rates, the yen and intervention needs. Japan Research Institute economist Takeshi Makita warned against treating the surplus as a permanent source.

The Industry Ministry was also proposing broader two-step lending through Japan Finance Corporation, including megabanks and regional lenders, and partial government absorption of lender losses. The measures would support Takaichi's ambition for ¥370 trillion of public and private investment across 17 strategic sectors through fiscal 2040. Keio University's Takero Doi warned that losses could ultimately reach the general account, while noting that banks combining state-backed and their own lending would retain incentives to assess risk. Takaichi pointed to previous-year bond issuance around ¥40 trillion as a benchmark for a similar approach to the next budget.

Currency forecasts reflect competing views of the rate environment facing that financing. TTT Moneycorp's Neil Parker expects the yen near 155 at year-end and 147 next year, with the BOJ raising its rate from 1.25% to at least 2%, possibly 2.25%, while the Fed stops around 4.00%-4.25%. He sees roughly another 50 basis points of interest-gap narrowing by the middle to latter part of next year. Parker said underlying inflation of 2.6% or more, against September's 2.4% excluding fresh food and energy, could accelerate the response. His outlook contrasts with another leading forecaster's projection of yen weakness toward 170.

New issuance continued across Asian currencies. Berkshire Hathaway mandated Mizuho and BofA for a potential yen benchmark sale, subject to conditions, as Japanese corporate issuance slowed after October supply widened spreads. China completed its previously announced Canadian green-sovereign offering: 4 billion yuan split equally between three- and five-year notes yielding 1.4% and 1.5%. Orders exceeded 59 billion yuan, about 14.75 times the deal, securing funding at the ministry's first offshore yuan issuance venue beyond Hong Kong, Macau and London.

In Europe, ministers advanced the ECB succession process toward a possible package covering the presidency and the seats of Isabel Schnabel and Philip Lane. A decision is targeted before year-end. Candidate Klaas Knot said the ECB could use its crisis tools, including large-scale purchases, against unwarranted, disorderly spread movements. He saw no major current transmission disruption and suggested only limited additional tightening might be needed because second-round effects remained contained. The remarks supplied a more bounded inflation assessment from a candidate generally viewed as hawkish, without changing current ECB policy.

## Oil Relief Runs Alongside Supply Vulnerability

Brent's fall to $92.17 and WTI's 4.90% decline to $86.38 extended the reduction in energy costs. Brent was 12.03% below its week-earlier level. Optimism about diplomacy supported the move, while Secretary of State Marco Rubio continued to describe Iran's negotiating demands as unacceptable. Iran said it was not obliged to submit to full nuclear monitoring while threatened with U.S. attacks, leaving a central obstacle in the negotiations unresolved.

A Reuters survey added evidence of recovering physical production. The 11 OPEC members covered produced an estimated 22.87 million barrels a day in October, up 1.38 million from September. Saudi Arabia, Kuwait and Iraq led the gains. Output had recovered to about 90% of February's pre-war 25.48 million barrels a day. Earlier quota increases had not translated fully into production amid conflict and export restrictions, including the U.S. blockade of Iranian shipments.

Saudi state media reported a new strike on the East-West pipeline in the Medina region. An Energy Ministry source said a limited fire had been extinguished, with no injuries and operations uninterrupted. The route carries approximately 4 million barrels a day diverted toward Yanbu because of Hormuz restrictions, roughly 4% of global supply according to Reuters. Its continued operation preserves a major alternative export path even as the attack underscores infrastructure exposure.

Russian fuel supply faced a different disruption. Reuters reported renewed regional rationing after Ukrainian attacks targeted at least eight major refineries over two weeks. Leningrad Governor Alexander Drozdenko reported an overnight strike on Kirishi, Russia's second-largest refinery. Karelia limited highway purchases to 30 litres of gasoline or 50 litres of diesel and suspended sales into canisters. Reduced refinery availability could constrain product exports, including previously discussed diesel arrangements, while the scale of the latest national production loss remained unquantified.

European governments were responding to the affordability consequences of still-elevated energy costs. Italy approved an 18-month scheme beginning in January to reimburse gas-fired generators for the positive difference between TTF gas prices and €58.9 per MWh. Energy Minister Pichetto Fratin estimated average electricity-cost relief of about €15 per MWh. Higher system charges on some consumers and contributions from producers would finance much of the intervention; energy companies objected to restrictions on passing costs through. TTF was around €82 per MWh Monday after exceeding €104 in October.

The Czech government approved a legislative proposal for intervention during exceptional energy-market stress, subject to parliament. It would allow the budget to absorb some electricity and gas network costs and use an excess-profit levy on producers to help fund relief. Italy's approved temporary reimbursement and the Czech proposal allocate energy costs differently among households, producers and government. Their effects on bills depend on the measures' operation alongside wholesale prices.

## Forward Market Significance

October U.S. CPI arrives Tuesday at 8:30 a.m. Eastern. Consensus expects a 0.3% monthly headline increase after 0.6%, and 0.2% core inflation after 0.3%. Year-over-year comparisons will not be published because the prior-year shutdown disrupted data collection. After Goolsbee's warning about demand overheating and Barkin's account of broad cost pass-through, the distribution of monthly inflation across services and goods will matter alongside the anticipated headline slowdown.

Tuesday also brings NFIB small-business optimism, expected at 97.7 against 97.9, followed by ADP's weekly employment reading. Christopher Waller, Lorie Logan, Michelle Bowman and Jeffrey Schmid have scheduled appearances. Their assessments will add to the policy debate over persistent inflation, the pace of tightening and the extent to which financial-market volatility changes the demand outlook.

Treasury will sell $42 billion of 10-year notes Tuesday at 1 p.m. Eastern, followed by $25 billion of 30-year bonds Thursday. Wednesday's Veterans Day closure separates those sales. Corporate funding tests include Fox's prospective bond sale, Fullscript's expected Tuesday acquisition close and negotiations over replacement direct lending, and the Qualtrics marketing effort. These transactions will show how the renewed appetite for risk translates into actual financing terms across established issuers, sponsor-backed companies and the AI capital-raising pipeline.

overall_summary.session_narrative:
Treasuries reversed part of their recent rally as technology shares recovered, reducing haven demand, while investors rebuilt expectations for Fed tightening and absorbed refunding supply. The 2-year yield rose 5 basis points to 4.5615%, and the 10-year increased 2.46 basis points to 4.882%, flattening the curve. The 10-year real yield rose 4.38 basis points as breakeven inflation fell 1.92 basis points, cushioning the nominal selloff.

The Nasdaq 100 gained 3.40%, and Brent fell 6.26% to $92.17 on hopes for progress toward ending the Iran war. Cheaper energy supported equities and restrained inflation compensation. Goolsbee warned that AI construction was beginning to resemble demand overheating, while Barkin described broad corporate cost pressures and favored careful further tightening. The $58 billion 3-year Treasury sale cleared slightly above pre-auction yields, with record direct participation.

U.S. high-yield spreads tightened noticeably, but financing terms remained uneven. Fox prepared roughly $8 billion of investment-grade refinancing, and Ecopetrol completed a $2 billion dollar issue; banks explored selling nearly $2 billion of Qualtrics debt around 85 cents on the dollar. Tuesday's CPI release and 10-year auction will test the inflation outlook and demand for new duration.
